title: APAC night shift — on-call handoff and shift log (2026-03-12)
content:
Shift window: 2026-03-12 20:00 SGT to 2026-03-13 04:00 SGT
Owner (outgoing): Aisha Kapoor
Owner (incoming): Tomás Rivera (primary), Mei Chen (backup)
Slack on-call channel: #sre-oncall (use @sre-oncall for page notifications)
Pager escalation policy: follow SRE escalation matrix v2 (see Confluence link above)

--- SUMMARY / HIGHLIGHTS ---
- Quiet start, then two distinct issues: (1) short-lived tokenization service latency spike impacting hosted API text-generation endpoints (~35m total impact window, degraded 20–30% p50->p95); (2) embeddings indexing job failures on a Dedicated host due to transient NFS timeouts (restarted job, reassigned shards).
- No customer-facing incident page was required; we proactively posted to #customer-status for affected customers on dedicated capacity and to internal incident tracker.
- Primary mitigation actions completed during shift. Key follow-ups and a runbook draft created below.

--- INCIDENT A: tokenization-service latency spike (affects hosted API text-generation) ---
Timeline (SGT / UTC+8):
- ~20:12: First alert from Datadog: tokenization-service p95 latency > 600ms for 1 minute (alert threshold 400ms).
- 20:14: Pager triggered (rotation: me). Joined #sre-oncall and opened incident thread.
- 20:15–20:22: quick triage: CPU utilization on tokenizer pods increased; autoscaler did not add pods (HPA observed stalled scale-up).
- 20:23: Identified increased request fanout from a new internal batch-writer (infra change) that caused hot shards (same prefix).
- 20:25: Temporary mitigation: add request-rate limiter in envoy route (rolled config using canary, 1 node first) and restart batch-writer job to slow ramp.
- 20:30: p95 dropped from 820ms -> 380ms. Continued monitoring.
- 20:47: Full baseline restored. Closed pager at 20:52 after 40m.
What we did:
- Limited offending upstream traffic (envoy rate-limit for route) -> immediate relief.
- Restarted autoscaler controller pod to clear HPA stuck state (controller logs show 503 on metrics endpoint during 20:05–20:12).
- Opened ticket SRE-4123 to track root cause and interfacing change with batch-writer team.

Observed gaps / runbook notes:
- HPA stuck detection: our runbooks assume HPA will always scale within X minutes; add explicit health check / watchdog that alerts when HPA desired != actual for >2m.
- Envoy rate-limit recipe exists but not documented for tokenization route specifically. Need a snippet and rollback steps.
- Add query in dashboards to surface "shard hotness" metrics (requests per prefix) so ops can identify hot key patterns quicker.

Proposed runbook additions (short checklist):
1) On alert for tokenization p95 > threshold: check pod CPU/memory and HPA desired/actual.
2) Query "requests by prefix" dashboard for hot keys.
3) If HPA desired != actual: restart controller-manager and check metrics endpoint (logs: /var/logs/hpa-metrics).
4) If hot key detected: apply temporary envoy rate-limit on route (example config: confluence link).
5) If upstream spike present: coordinate with owner of upstream (see list below).

Owners for follow-ups:
- Add HPA watchdog alert: Jacob Lin -> INFRA-278
- Document envoy rate-limit recipe and add to runbook: Mei Chen -> (no ticket yet)
- Postmortem writeup for tokenization: Aisha Kapoor -> SRE-4123

--- INCIDENT B: embeddings-indexer job failures (Dedicated) ---
Timeline (SGT):
- 22:05: Long-running embeddings indexer job started failing with repeated "NFS: timeout" errors during shard write.
- 22:10: Pager to on-call; I took the lead and contacted Dedicated ops.
- 22:18: Identified transient network flaps between host and NFS subnet (packet loss at 0.5–1%).
- 22:25: Re-scheduled failing shards to healthy Dedicated hosts, restarted job.
- 22:45: Indexing resumed successfully; monitored until 23:05.

What we did:
- Rescheduled and restarted jobs to avoid the affected host.
- Ramp back write concurrency from 20 -> 8 to reduce NFS load while infra team investigates.

Gaps / notes: 
- No automatic reschedule for indexing jobs when filesystem errors occur; scheduler assumes infra is stable. Add 'failed-write' detection to the job runner so it can fail fast and reschedule.
- Need a health-check for NFS mounts that alerts before jobs attempt heavy writes.

Follow-ups: 
- Short term: add quick health probe in job runner (owner: Tomás Rivera) -> ticket SRE-4137 (create).
- Mid term: infra to investigate NFS subnet packet loss and put in compensating measures (owner: infra team, linked INFRA-279).

--- ON-CALL ACTIONS (completed) ---
- Restarted HPA controller pod (logs collected and uploaded to S3: s3://redwood-ops/sre/logs/hpa-controller-2026-03-12.log).
- Deployed envoy temporary route limiter in canary then full (config stored in repo PR linked above).
- Rescheduled embeddings indexer shards away from problematic host.

--- RUNBOOK DRAFT NOTES (content for new SRE runbook page) ---
Title: tokenization-service latency — on-call playbook (draft)
Purpose: Identify hot-shard caused latency and recover quickly with minimal customer impact.
Sections to include: detection -> triage -> containment -> remediation -> postmortem.
Important commands / queries to include (add to Confluence with copy/paste):
- kubectl get hpa -n inference tokenization-hpa -o wide
- grafana query (requests by prefix): alias(request.count.by_prefix)
- envoy rate-limit example snippet (yaml) and rollback steps
- how to restart HPA controller safely: systemctl restart hpa-controller; check metrics endpoint

--- FOLLOW-UPS / ACTION ITEMS (with owners & recommended due dates) ---
- SRE-4123 (Aisha) — write full postmortem and timeline, include graphs from Datadog, due 2026-03-16
- INFRA-278 (Jacob) — add HPA watchdog alert and test in staging, due 2026-03-17
- SRE-4137 (Tomás) — job-runner failed-write fast-fail and reschedule change, draft PR due 2026-03-19
- Document envoy limiter snippet and add to tokenization runbook (Mei) — due 2026-03-15
- Infra: investigate NFS packet loss and mitigation plan (infra team) — update by 2026-03-18

--- ESCALATION CONTACTS (quick list) ---
- Infra lead: Jacob Lin (pager) / slack @jacob.lin / +1-555-0188
- Serving runtime lead: Mei Chen / slack @mei / +1-555-0199
- Product-owner tokenization: Souvik Roy / slack @souvik / internal ext: x4621

--- NOTES FOR THE NEXT SHIFT (Tomás / Mei) ---
- Watch for follow-up PRs on envoy limiter and HPA watchdog testing in staging.
- Keep an eye on NFS metrics for Dedicated hosts over the next 72 hours; infra is running a longer capture.
- If tokenization p95 rises again but HPA is healthy, check for new upstreams or reruns of the batch-writer job — owners listed in SRE-4123.

--- QUICK LINKS ---
- Incident thread (internal): slack://channel/sre-incidents/thread/abcdef
- PR for emergency envoy limiter: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/842
- Postmortem draft placeholder: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=TOKEN-POSTMORTEM-DRAFT

End of handoff. Please ping in #sre-oncall if anything spikes.
Aisha (outgoing)
summary: Night shift notes capturing two incidents: tokenization latency spike due to HPA/ upstream hot-shard, and embeddings indexer NFS write failures. Mitigations applied; runbook draft and follow-ups created.
